query: For a selected high-entropy alloy whose superconducting behavior remains uncharacterized, what governs whether and how superconductivity emerges in the low-temperature test regime, and why? Propose one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison with the starting state, the observations expected relative to that baseline, the limits over which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The high configurational entropy of mixing (ΔSmix) in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) enhances the robustness of superconductivity under high pressure.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy (HEA) with a high configurational entropy of mixing (ΔSmix)
generation.mechanism: The high ΔSmix reduces the Gibbs free energy, stabilizing the phase and enhancing the robustness of superconductivity under high pressure.
generation.predicted_outcome: The superconducting transition temperature (Tc) remains relatively constant or increases with pressure in HEAs with high ΔSmix, whereas Tc decreases with pressure in low-entropy alloys.
generation.baseline: Low-entropy alloys (e.g., PbTe) with low ΔSmix
generation.boundary: The pressure range over which the hypothesis holds is limited by the stability of the crystal structure and the emergence of other phases.
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between ΔSmix, crystal structure, and superconducting properties is still unclear and requires further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) of an HEA with high ΔSmix under various pressures and compare it to a low-entropy alloy with low ΔSmix.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Tc decreases with pressure in the HEA with high ΔSmix, similar to low-entropy alloys, the hypothesis is falsified.

Furthermore, the robustness of superconductivity to extremely high pressure (HP), for pressures up to 190 GPa, in an HEA, (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33, was observed. The high configurational entropy of mixing (ΔSmix) reduces the Gibbs’s free energy, and therefore stabilization of the phase is expected. The equation for calculating the Gibb’s free energy is ΔG = ΔH − TΔSmix, where ΔH is the enthalpy and T is the absolute temperature. ΔSmix can be calculated using the equation ΔSmix = − R ∑i cilnci, where, R is the gas constant and ci is the atomic ratio of the element (i). The discovery of the robustness of superconductivity under an extremely high pressure was considered to be related to the high ΔSmix, but similar robustness of superconductivity under an extremely high pressure and a high transition temperature (Tc) of 19 K was observed in a low-entropy Nb–Ti alloy. ## Crystal structure
Figure 3a–c show the pressure-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) patterns for the PbTe, AgPbBiTe3, and AgInSnPbBiTe5 samples, respectively. For all the SXRD patterns, we performed the Rietveld refinement to confirm the structural type and to evaluate the lattice constant. See Tables S1–S3 and Figs. S4–S6 for details on refinements. On the basis of the refinement results, we established structural phase diagrams under high pressure (Fig. 3d–f) by plotting the pressure dependence of volume per unit formula (Z). For PbTe, the structural transition from NaCl-type to Pnma occurs at around 6.80 GPa, and the second transition to CsCl-type takes place at 14.28 GPa. Since the transition gradually occurred, the phase diagram contains mixed phases. The results on PbTe are consistent with the previous work by Li et al..
